subject: math
title: Multiplication and Division: Equal Groups, Arrays, Sharing and Grouping
seo_title: Grade 3 Math Multiplication and Division Worksheets (BC Curriculum, Free, Answer Key)
meta_desc: Free Grade 3 math worksheets on multiplication and division concepts: equal groups, arrays, repeated addition and skip counting, sharing and grouping, and word problems about hockey cards, canoes and field trips. 100 questions with an answer key, following the BC curriculum.
key_big: Multiplication counts equal groups. Division splits a total into equal groups.
key_sub: 3 × 4 means 3 groups of 4: 4 + 4 + 4 = 12, not 3 + 4 = 7. 12 ÷ 3 = 4: share 12 into 3 groups, or make groups of 3 and count them.
body_html:
Equal groups

Multiplication counts equal groups. 3 groups of 4 is 3 × 4. The first number tells how many groups. The second number tells how many in each group.

Arrays

An array puts equal groups in rows. Count the rows. Then count one row.

Turn the array a quarter turn and you get 5 rows of 3. It is still 15 dots, so 3 × 5 = 5 × 3.

Repeated addition and skip counting

Multiplication is a fast way to add the same number again and again. You can also skip count on a number line.

Repeated addition

What is 4 × 6?

4 groups of 6: 6 + 6 + 6 + 6 = 24.

Answer: 24

Division: sharing and grouping

Sharing: you know how many groups. Give the items out one at a time. 12 shared on 3 plates is 4 on each plate.

Grouping: you know how many in each group. 12 in groups of 3 makes 4 groups. You can also take away 3 again and again: 12 − 3 − 3 − 3 − 3 = 0. That is 4 groups. Both ways give 12 ÷ 3 = 4. Always start with the total.

Divide with a times fact

What is 20 ÷ 5?

Think: 5 × ☐ = 20. 5 × 4 = 20.

Answer: 4

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Adding instead of multiplying (3 × 4 = 7)3 × 4 means 3 groups of 4: 4 + 4 + 4 = 12
Giving the number in one group, not the total (3 groups of 4 = 4)Count all the items: 3 × 4 = 12
Mixing up groups and items (3 groups of 4 drawn as 4 groups of 3)The first number is the number of groups
Dividing the wrong way (4 ÷ 20 = 5)Start with the total: 20 ÷ 4 = 5
Mixing up sharing and grouping“Among 4” means 4 groups. “Groups of 4” means 4 in each group

faq.q: What multiplication and division does Grade 3 learn in the BC math curriculum?
faq.a: In the BC curriculum, Grade 3 students learn multiplication and division concepts. They use equal groups, arrays, repeated addition and skip counting to multiply, and sharing and grouping to divide.

faq.q: Do Grade 3 students in BC need to memorize times tables?
faq.a: Grade 3 in BC focuses on understanding what multiplication and division mean. Learning the multiplication and division facts to 100 is a Grade 4 goal, so early practice with groups and skip counting helps.

faq.q: What is the difference between sharing and grouping in division?
faq.a: In sharing you know the number of groups and find how many go in each, like 12 shared on 3 plates. In grouping you know how many go in each group and find the number of groups, like 12 in groups of 3. Both give 12 ÷ 3 = 4.

faq.q: Why does my child use arrays for multiplication?
faq.a: An array shows equal rows, so students can see that 3 rows of 5 is 5 + 5 + 5 = 15. Turning the array also shows that 3 × 5 = 5 × 3.

items.e: 5 groups of 2: 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 = 10. 7 comes from 5 + 2. 2 is only one plate.

items.q: How many counters are there altogether?
items.e: There are 2 groups. Each group has 5 counters. Count by 5s: 5, 10. So 2 groups of 5 = 2 × 5 = 10.

items.q: Hana has 4 bags. Each bag has 6 apples. Which shows how many apples she has?
items.e: 4 bags with 6 in each is 4 groups of 6. That is 4 × 6 = 24. 4 + 6 only joins the two numbers.

items.q: Nadia makes 3 groups of 7 shells. How many shells does she use?
items.e: 3 groups of 7: 7 + 7 + 7 = 21. 10 comes from 3 + 7. 7 is only one group.

items.q: Which number sentence matches the picture?
items.e: There are 5 groups of 2: 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 = 10. That is 5 × 2 = 10. 5 + 2 only adds the two numbers.

items.q: Which picture shows 3 groups of 4?
items.e: 3 groups of 4 means 3 groups with 4 in each group. D shows this. 4 groups of 3 mixes up the groups and the counters in each group. The other pictures do not have equal groups or have the wrong number of groups.

items.q: How many counters are there altogether?
items.e: There are 3 groups. Each group has 4 counters. Count by 4s: 4, 8, 12. So 3 groups of 4 = 3 × 4 = 12.

items.q: Which has the same answer as 5 × 3?
items.e: Turn the array a quarter turn. 5 rows of 3 become 3 rows of 5. The dots do not change, so 5 × 3 = 3 × 5 = 15. 3 × 5 has the same answer.
There are 4 rows of 4. Count by 4s: 4, 8, 12, 16. So 4 × 4 = 16.

items.q: Which number sentence matches this array?
items.e: Count the rows: 2. Count one row: 6. 2 rows of 6 is 2 × 6 = 12. 2 + 6 only adds the two numbers. It does not count the dots.

items.q: This array shows 2 × 7 = 14. Which other number sentence also matches it?
items.e: Turn the array a quarter turn. 2 rows of 7 become 7 rows of 2. The number of dots does not change, so 7 × 2 = 14.

items.e: The order can change. The answer stays the same. 6 × 4 = 4 × 6, so the missing number is 6. Both are 24.

items.q: Which has the same answer as 2 × 9?
items.e: Turn the array a quarter turn. 2 rows of 9 become 9 rows of 2. The dots do not change, so 2 × 9 = 9 × 2 = 18. 9 × 2 has the same answer.
Rows go across. Count down the side: there are 3 rows. 6 is the number of dots in each row.

items.q: How many dots are in this array?
items.e: There are 2 rows of 4. Count by 4s: 4, 8. So 2 × 4 = 8.

Look along one row from left to right: 8 dots. 2 is the number of rows.

items.q: Which has the same answer as 4 × 7?
items.e: Turn the array a quarter turn. 4 rows of 7 become 7 rows of 4. The dots do not change, so 4 × 7 = 7 × 4 = 28. 7 × 4 has the same answer.
Rows go across. Count down the side: there are 4 rows. 7 is the number of dots in each row.

items.q: Which has the same answer as 3 × 10?
items.e: Turn the array a quarter turn. 3 rows of 10 become 10 rows of 3. The dots do not change, so 3 × 10 = 10 × 3 = 30. 10 × 3 has the same answer.

items.q: This array shows 3 × 5 = 15. Which other number sentence also matches it?
items.e: Turn the array a quarter turn. 3 rows of 5 become 5 rows of 3. The number of dots does not change, so 5 × 3 = 15.
Count the rows: 5. Count one row: 8. 5 rows of 8 is 5 × 8 = 40. 5 + 8 only adds the two numbers. It does not count the dots.

items.q: Owen says 3 × 4 = 7. What did he do?
items.e: 3 + 4 = 7. But 3 × 4 means 3 groups of 4: 4 + 4 + 4 = 12. Owen added instead of multiplying.

items.q: Which is the same as 7 + 7?
items.e: Count the 7s: there are 2 of them. 2 groups of 7 is 2 × 7 = 14.

items.q: Count by 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20, ☐. What number comes next?
items.e: Each number is 5 more than the one before. 20 + 5 = 25.

items.q: Count by 3s: 3, 6, 9, 12, ☐. What number comes next?
items.e: Each number is 3 more than the one before. 12 + 3 = 15.

items.q: Which number sentence matches the jumps?
items.e: There are 5 jumps of 4. Skip count: 4, 8, 12, 16, 20. So 5 × 4 = 20. Count the jumps (the arrows), not the marks.

items.q: Which is the same as 3 + 3 + 3 + 3 + 3?
items.e: Count the 3s: there are 5 of them. 5 groups of 3 is 5 × 3 = 15.

items.q: Ji-woo skip counts by 5s to find 6 × 5. Where should she stop?
items.e: Say 6 numbers: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30. Stop at 30. 25 is only 5 counts. 11 is 6 + 5.

items.q: Which addition is the same as 4 × 9?
items.e: 4 × 9 means 4 groups of 9. Add 9, 4 times: 9 + 9 + 9 + 9 = 36.

items.q: Which is the same as 8 + 8 + 8?
items.e: Count the 8s: there are 3 of them. 3 groups of 8 is 3 × 8 = 24.

items.q: Which addition is the same as 5 × 6?
items.e: 5 × 6 means 5 groups of 6. Add 6, 5 times: 6 + 6 + 6 + 6 + 6 = 30.

items.q: Count by 2s: 2, 4, 6, 8, ☐. What number comes next?
items.e: Each number is 2 more than the one before. 8 + 2 = 10.

items.q: Which number sentence matches the jumps?
items.e: There are 6 jumps of 3. Skip count: 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18. So 6 × 3 = 18. Count the jumps (the arrows), not the marks.

items.q: Count by 10s: 10, 20, 30, ☐. What number comes next?
items.e: Each number is 10 more than the one before. 30 + 10 = 40.

items.q: Which is the right answer to 2 × 5?
items.e: 2 × 5 means 2 groups of 5: 5 + 5 = 10. 7 is 2 + 5. 25 is 5 groups of 5. 3 is 5 − 2.

items.q: Mei skip counts by 4s. She says 4, 8, 12, 16. Which multiplication does this show?
items.e: She says 4 numbers, so there are 4 groups of 4. The last number is the total: 4 × 4 = 16.

items.q: Which number sentence matches the jumps?
items.e: There are 4 jumps of 5. Skip count: 5, 10, 15, 20. So 4 × 5 = 20. Count the jumps (the arrows), not the marks.

items.q: Which is the same as 10 + 10 + 10 + 10?
items.e: Count the 10s: there are 4 of them. 4 groups of 10 is 4 × 10 = 40.

items.q: Which addition is the same as 3 × 8?
items.e: 3 × 8 means 3 groups of 8. Add 8, 3 times: 8 + 8 + 8 = 24.

items.q: Which number sentence matches the jumps?
items.e: There are 7 jumps of 2. Skip count: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14. So 7 × 2 = 14. Count the jumps (the arrows), not the marks.

items.q: Which is the same as 6 + 6 + 6 + 6?
items.e: Count the 6s: there are 4 of them. 4 groups of 6 is 4 × 6 = 24.

items.q: Share these 10 counters equally on 2 plates. How many go on each plate?
items.e: Sharing: give the counters out one at a time until none are left. Each of the 2 plates gets 5. 10 ÷ 2 = 5.

items.q: 16 counters are put in groups of 4. How many groups are there?
items.e: Grouping: you know there are 4 in each group. Count the rings: 4 groups. So 16 ÷ 4 = 4.

items.q: 18 counters are put in groups of 3. How many groups are there?
items.e: Grouping: you know there are 3 in each group. Count the rings: 6 groups. So 18 ÷ 3 = 6.

items.q: What is 30 ÷ 5? Think: 5 × ☐ = 30.
items.e: Think multiplication: 5 × ☐ = 30. 5 × 6 = 30, so 30 ÷ 5 = 6.

items.q: 12 counters are put in groups of 2. How many groups are there?
items.e: Grouping: you know there are 2 in each group. Count the rings: 6 groups. So 12 ÷ 2 = 6.

items.q: Sofia takes away 3 again and again: 12 − 3 − 3 − 3 − 3 = 0. Which division does this show?
items.e: Count how many times 3 is taken away: 4 times. So 12 has 4 groups of 3: 12 ÷ 3 = 4. Do not count the 12 at the start.

items.q: 14 counters are shared equally on 2 plates. Which division matches the picture?
items.e: 14 counters are shared on 2 plates. Each plate has 7. That is 14 ÷ 2 = 7. Always start with the total, 14. 2 ÷ 14 is the wrong way around.
Sharing: give the counters out one at a time until none are left. Each of the 4 plates gets 5. 20 ÷ 4 = 5.

items.q: Which one is grouping?
items.e: Grouping means you know how many go in each group. “Bags of 5” tells you there are 5 in each bag. 20 ÷ 5 = 4 bags. Sharing among 5 bags is sharing: you know the number of bags.
Sharing among 3 plates means 3 plates, all the same. B has 3 plates of 5. 5 plates of 3 is groups of 3. 6, 5 and 4 are not equal, and 3 plates of 4 is only 12.

items.q: Share these 12 counters equally on 3 plates. How many go on each plate?
items.e: Sharing: give the counters out one at a time until none are left. Each of the 3 plates gets 4. 12 ÷ 3 = 4.

items.q: Share these 15 counters equally on 5 plates. How many go on each plate?
items.e: Sharing: give the counters out one at a time until none are left. Each of the 5 plates gets 3. 15 ÷ 5 = 3.

items.q: 20 counters are put in groups of 5. How many groups are there?
items.e: Grouping: you know there are 5 in each group. Count the rings: 4 groups. So 20 ÷ 5 = 4.

items.q: Sofia takes away 5 again and again: 20 − 5 − 5 − 5 − 5 = 0. Which division does this show?
items.e: Count how many times 5 is taken away: 4 times. So 20 has 4 groups of 5: 20 ÷ 5 = 4. Do not count the 20 at the start.

items.q: Sofia takes away 4 again and again: 16 − 4 − 4 − 4 − 4 = 0. Which division does this show?
items.e: Count how many times 4 is taken away: 4 times. So 16 has 4 groups of 4: 16 ÷ 4 = 4. Do not count the 16 at the start.

items.q: Which one is sharing?
c: Put 18 hockey cards in piles of 3.
items.e: Sharing means you know how many groups. “Among 3 friends” tells you there are 3 groups. 18 ÷ 3 = 6 cards each. Piles of 3 is grouping: you know how many go in each pile.
24 counters are shared on 4 plates. Each plate has 6. That is 24 ÷ 4 = 6. Always start with the total, 24. 4 ÷ 24 is the wrong way around.
Think multiplication: 10 × ☐ = 40. 10 × 4 = 40, so 40 ÷ 10 = 4.
21 counters are shared on 3 plates. Each plate has 7. That is 21 ÷ 3 = 7. Always start with the total, 21. 3 ÷ 21 is the wrong way around.

items.q: What is 18 ÷ 2? Think: 2 × ☐ = 18.
items.e: Think multiplication: 2 × ☐ = 18. 2 × 9 = 18, so 18 ÷ 2 = 9.

items.q: Wei shares 20 strawberries equally between 2 bowls. How many strawberries go in each bowl?
items.e: Sharing between 2 bowls: 20 ÷ 2. 2 × 10 = 20, so each bowl gets 10. (40 comes from 20 × 2.)

items.q: Arjun shares 24 hockey cards equally among 4 friends. How many cards does each friend get?
items.e: Sharing among 4 friends: 24 ÷ 4. 4 × 6 = 24, so each friend gets 6 cards.

items.q: On a field trip to Stanley Park, 27 students walk in groups of 3. How many groups are there?
items.e: Grouping in 3s: 27 ÷ 3. 3 × 9 = 27, so there are 9 groups.

items.q: Mateo has 9 toonies. A toonie is worth $2. How much money does he have?
items.e: 9 toonies is 9 groups of $2: 9 × $2 = $18. $11 comes from adding 9 + 2.

items.q: A pack of hockey cards has 5 cards. Liam buys 4 packs. How many cards does he get?
items.e: There are 4 equal groups of 5, so multiply: 4 × 5 = 20. Adding 4 + 5 = 9 only joins the two numbers.

items.q: At a soccer tournament in Kelowna, each team brings 9 players. 4 teams play on Saturday morning. How many players is that?
items.e: There are 4 equal groups of 9, so multiply: 4 × 9 = 36. Adding 4 + 9 = 13 only joins the two numbers.

items.q: Simran reads 10 pages each day. How many days does it take her to read 50 pages?
items.e: How many 10s make 50? 50 ÷ 10 = 5 days. Check: 5 × 10 = 50.

items.q: For the Terry Fox Run, Zara walks 3 laps of the field each day for 5 days. Owen walks 10 laps in all. How many more laps does Zara walk?
items.e: Step 1: Zara walks 5 × 3 = 15 laps. Step 2: 15 − 10 = 5 more laps. (15 is only step 1.)

items.q: At lunch, 8 students sit at each table. There are 5 full tables. How many students are at the tables?
items.e: There are 5 equal groups of 8, so multiply: 5 × 8 = 40. Adding 5 + 8 = 13 only joins the two numbers.

items.q: Noah buys 3 hot chocolates at the rink. Each one costs $2. He pays with a $10 bill. How much change does he get?
items.e: Step 1: cost: 3 × $2 = $6. Step 2: change: $10 − $6 = $4. ($6 is the cost, not the change.)

items.q: The class sets up chairs for the winter concert. There are 6 rows with 8 chairs in each row. How many chairs are there?
items.e: There are 6 equal groups of 8, so multiply: 6 × 8 = 48. Adding 6 + 8 = 14 only joins the two numbers.

items.q: At summer camp on Vancouver Island, 7 canoes go out on the lake. Each canoe holds 3 people. How many people can the canoes hold?
items.e: There are 7 equal groups of 3, so multiply: 7 × 3 = 21. Adding 7 + 3 = 10 only joins the two numbers.

items.q: Ethan has 40¢ in nickels. A nickel is 5¢. How many nickels does he have?
items.e: How many 5s make 40? 40 ÷ 5. 5 × 8 = 40, so he has 8 nickels.

items.q: Kai has 3 bags of marbles with 8 marbles in each bag. He shares all the marbles equally among 4 friends. How many marbles does each friend get?
items.e: Step 1: 3 × 8 = 24 marbles. Step 2: 24 ÷ 4 = 6, because 4 × 6 = 24. (24 is only step 1.)

items.q: In gym class, 35 students make teams of 5. How many teams are there?
items.e: Grouping in 5s: 35 ÷ 5. 5 × 7 = 35, so there are 7 teams.

items.q: 15 students go on a field trip to Grouse Mountain. Each parent driver takes 3 students. How many cars are needed?
items.e: Groups of 3: 15 ÷ 3. 3 × 5 = 15, so 5 cars are needed. (45 comes from 15 × 3.)

items.q: There are 32 chairs in the library. They are in 4 equal rows. How many chairs are in each row?
items.e: 32 chairs in 4 equal rows: 32 ÷ 4. 4 × 8 = 32, so each row has 8 chairs.

items.q: Chloe helps plant cedar seedlings. She plants 5 rows with 6 seedlings in each row. How many seedlings does she plant?
items.e: There are 5 equal groups of 6, so multiply: 5 × 6 = 30. Adding 5 + 6 = 11 only joins the two numbers.

items.q: Bald eagles sit in the trees by the Fraser River. There are 3 eagles in each of 8 trees. How many eagles are there?
items.e: There are 8 equal groups of 3, so multiply: 8 × 3 = 24. Adding 8 + 3 = 11 only joins the two numbers.

items.q: Ava has 4 packs of stickers. Each pack has 5 stickers. She gives 6 stickers to her brother. How many stickers does she have left?
items.e: Step 1: 4 × 5 = 20 stickers. Step 2: 20 − 6 = 14 stickers left. (3 comes from 4 + 5 − 6.)
